positions.commentary: The speaker states that Microsoft invented the closed source business model and benefited from open source research, but argues AI companies should not be against open source.
The speaker notes that open source existed even when IBM existed, implying IBM is not inherently against open source.
The speaker mentions AT&T became the national phone company and was a branch of the government, but offers no specific view on the company's current stance.

thesis: The episode argues that AI companies should not be against open source, noting that Microsoft invented the closed source business model while benefiting from open source research. It also suggests that IBM is not inherently against open source, as open source existed during IBM's time, and mentions AT&T's historical status as a government branch without offering a specific view on its current stance.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Microsoft invented the closed source business model and benefited from open source research, but argues AI companies should not be against open source.
claims.quote: And Microsoft where we were a closed source, Bill Gates invented the closed source business model. And so we lived through the rise of HTTP and Apache and web and Linux and all of this other stuff. But there is a role for open source.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that open source existed even when IBM existed, implying IBM is not inherently against open source.
claims.quote: And most importantly, the open source existed even when Microsoft existed, even when IBM existed. And so there's no reason why the AI company should be against open source.
